children: Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) is set to significantly reduce its Russian crude oil purchases in November as higher freight costs and elevated premiums make West Asian grades more commercially attractive, signalling a shift in the state-run refiner's sourcing strategy.

Russian crude accounted for around 37% of BPCL's crude sourcing mix in the July-September quarter. However, the company has cut purchases of Russian cargoes for November as shipping costs have risen, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, BPCL's head of finance, said on Monday. "October, our requirement from Russia has slightly come down, but in November, cargoes from Russia have reduced significantly due to their commercial viability. Mainly due to the increase in freight, we are not getting good offers from Russia," Gupta told analysts on a call.

The company expects supplies from West Asia to increase in October and November compared with the first quarter, when disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz affected supplies from the region. "October-November also, we are expecting similar lengths of higher volume from West Asia.

title: BPCL to Cut Russian Oil as West Asian Crude Gets Cheaper
